body: Flag: POOR (Shahra era) / MIXED (Patanjali era). Ruchi Soya, an edible-oil major run by the Shahra family, over-borrowed and lost money on commodity bets and was admitted to IBC (Dec-2017; ~Rs 12,000 cr debt). Patanjali Ayurved won with a ~Rs 4,350 cr plan (2019); after relisting in Jan-2020 only ~1.1% of shares were public, and the stock rose from ~Rs 17 to over Rs 1,500 within months -- a thin-float price not reflecting fundamentals (market cap briefly exceeding many FMCG majors). The Mar-2022 FPO (Rs 4,300 cr) saw SEBI ask the company to let investors withdraw bids after unsolicited SMS messages promoting the issue circulated. Public float stayed below 25% (19.18% after FPO), so NSE/BSE froze 29.25 cr promoter shares (80.82% of equity) in Mar-2023 for MPS non-compliance; Patanjali Ayurved sold ~2.53 cr shares by OFS (Jul-2024) to reach 73.82% promoter holding. Renamed Patanjali Foods; absorbed Patanjali Ayurved's food business (2022, Rs 690 cr) and later its home & personal care business -- related-party acquisitions from the promoter that need independent valuation scrutiny. Patanjali Ayurved separately faced Supreme Court contempt proceedings over misleading ads (2024). Status Nov-2026: MPS compliant; watch further RPT acquisitions from the unlisted Patanjali Ayurved and the pricing of those deals.

data.red_flags: thin float post-IBC; FPO SMS episode; MPS freeze; RPT business transfers from promoter
data.status_2026: MPS compliant; RPTs with Patanjali Ayurved continue

title: Ruchi Soya (Shahra family) → Patanjali Foods (Patanjali/Ramdev) — governance history

body: Flag: POOR (pending SEBI case; interim findings, not final). Bengaluru gold refiner/jeweller reporting very large revenues (often Rs 2-3 lakh cr+ consolidated, largely via Swiss refiner Valcambi, bought 2015) at razor-thin margins, with limited segment/geography disclosure and a promoter holding ~54%. Long-standing analyst concerns: revenue quality, cash conversion, related-party trading, and frequent auditor changes; a 2023-24 PLI-linked battery venture (Elest/ACC Energy Storage) whose own auditor later resigned citing regulatory reasons. Regulator action: SEBI appointed BDO India as forensic auditor (Dec-2024); per SEBI's 109-page ex-parte interim order (3-Jun-2026), the forensic auditor was denied access to key records, ERP systems and journal data, and SEBI alleged standalone revenue was overstated by ~Rs 12,557 cr over FY21-FY24 (headlines cite a far larger cumulative 'misrepresentation' figure); promoter Rajesh Mehta was barred from dealing in the company's securities; SEBI ordered a fresh forensic audit and referred statutory auditors' conduct to NFRA (which reportedly opened a probe). The company said it would cooperate and not challenge the interim order, while disputing the allegations. SEBI confirmed its interim directions (Oct-2026). Early signals (visible for years): revenue far out of proportion to assets/employees, non-cooperation with information requests, opaque overseas subsidiary, low dividend relative to reported profits, and turnover-vs-cash-flow gaps. Lesson: when a forensic auditor reports non-cooperation, treat it as a stronger signal than any single number.

data.regulator_findings: SEBI interim Jun-2026 (confirmed Oct-2026): alleged Rs 12,557 cr revenue overstatement; forensic non-cooperation
